title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
claim: Baseline methods stall at a residual gap from the preference-optimal point; ours drives it to near machine precision for every preference.
layout: 2 rows by 5 columns, one per algorithm, trajectories above and convergence curves below, shared legend
description: A 2×5 grid of plots with one column per algorithm: EPO, PNG, FERERO, FOOPS and ParetoM³ (the last is the proposed method). The top row shows objective-space trajectories in (f1, f2). Each plot has a black quarter-circle Pareto front. Dashed preference rays in blue, green, red, cyan and magenta start at the origin. Colored trajectories run from a shared initial point, a blue dot near (1,1), to star-shaped output points on the front. The bottom row has log-scale plots of normalized distance to the preference-optimal objective values against outer iterations. In the baseline columns the curves plateau between roughly 1e-2 and 1e-5. In the ParetoM³ column the curves oscillate and fall steadily to about 1e-7. A shared legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Comparison of preference-guided algorithms on the synthetic benchmark. The top row shows the trajectories in the objective space, and the bottom row reports the norm-normalized distance to the preference-optimal objective values. Different colors correspond to different preference vectors, and each column corresponds to one algorithm.
abstract: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. We further develop ParetoM$^3$, a single-loop first-order algorithm for computing stationary solutions of the resulting M$^3$ problem. Under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption, we prove that ParetoM$^3$ finds an $Îµ$-stationary point of the M$^3$ problem that is also approximately weakly Pareto optimal for the original multi-objective problem when the penalty parameter is sufficiently large, with explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates. We also show that this stationarity notion recovers existing optimality criteria, including approximate preference stationarity and approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, under the same assumptions used in prior works. Experiments on a synthetic benchmark, image classification, regression, and math reasoning demonstrate that ParetoM$^3$ reliably attains preferred weak Pareto optimal solutions while achieving strong practical performance. Code is available at https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3.
